To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a calorie supply of about 35 kcal/kg BW/day, a protein supply of about 1.2-1.3 g N/ kg BW/day and an amino acid supply about 1.25-1.35 g/kg BW/day are required for the optimal nutritional therapy of polytraumatizied patients.
the optimum N-supply for the N-balance after severe trauma is about 0.2 to 0.3 g/kg BW/day and that the calorie supply excreted a slight N-sparin effect.

the cumulative N-balances after moderate trauma are positive, and after major trauma are negative, when the N-supply is less than 0.2 and greater than 0.3 g/kg BW/day; and that the N-balance is positive after severe trauma when the N-supplies is about 0.2 (or 1.25) g N/kg BW/ day.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a mathematical description of the cumulative N-balances in relation to the calorie and N-supples after trauma.
the influence of calorie and nitrogen supply after severe trauma on nitrogen balance.
the question of the influence of post-traumatic calorie and N-suppliy upon the cumulative N- balance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-balance is decisively influenced by the N-supply and that a supply of 0.2 to 0.3 g/kg BW/day is necessary for the posttraumatic period.
a calorie and N-supplementation after moderate and severe trauma of at least 20 kcal/kg BW/day, and 0.15-0.2 g N/kg BW/d should be recommended.
the N-balance after moderate trauma is only marginally influenced by the calorie supply and is mainly determined by the N-supply.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-supplies recommended for posttraumatic nutritional therapy are too small.

a calorie supply of about 30 kcal/kg BW/ day is necessary for the maintenance of the basal energy metabolism and the N-supplies must be about 0.25-0.3 N/kg BW/day in order to achieve a positive N-balance after trauma.
, in order to prevent a negative cumulative N-balance in patients with a severe trauma, the N-supply should be increased to about 0.2 to 0.3 g/kg BW/day.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a posttraumatic N-supply of 0.15-0.20 g/kg BW/day and a calorie supply of 20-30 g/kg BW/day are necessary to achieve a positive cumulative N-balance.
the N-supplies of the patients should be adapted to their individual requirements.
the N-balance is influenced by the calorie and the amino acid supply.
